source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A single, brief seizure episode lasting less than a minute total in duration, rather than the more prolonged activity this particular condition actually involves","B":"Continuous seizure activity lasting beyond a specific time threshold (commonly 5 minutes or more), or repeated seizures without full recovery of consciousness between episodes","C":"Seizure activity that is generally expected to resolve entirely on its own, without any need for clinical concern or active team intervention at any point","D":"A condition generally considered to lack any clearly established clinical definition within current neurological practice and treatment guidelines"}}
source_row.rationale: Status epilepticus is generally defined as continuous seizure activity lasting beyond a specific time threshold (commonly defined as 5 minutes or more in current definitions), or repeated seizures without full recovery of consciousness between episodes, representing a neurological emergency requiring prompt treatment.
